name: Meridian Monorail
description: A sleek elevated monorail connecting Tier 3-5 districts — the corporate spires, the financial center, the upscale residential towers. Clean, climate-controlled, biometric boarding. It runs above the L-train both literally and socially. You need a registered identity and a minimum Φ500 wallet balance to board. The cars are quiet. The seats are padded. It is everything the L-train is not, and that is the point.
cost: Φ15 per ride, Φ400 monthly pass, Φ500 minimum wallet balance required
armament: None visible. Integrated crowd suppression system (classified).
common_usage: Corporate commuters, executive transport, anyone who can afford to avoid the L-train.
story_hooks: A glitch in the biometric gate lets a Tier 1 resident board — they ride the entire loop and see a city they never knew existed
The monorail runs through a sealed section of track between two towers where it goes dark for eleven seconds and no one talks about why
physical_description: Sleek titanium-composite pods suspended on a carbon-fiber rail, their hulls a pristine pearl-white that catches neon bleed from the city below. Interior walls are brushed steel and climate-controlled polymer, with ergonomic seating upholstered in synthetic leather that shows no wear. The biometric scanner at each entrance glows soft blue, a gentle reminder of access denied.
visual_prompt: elevated monorail pod, pearl-white titanium composite, carbon-fiber rail, neo-noir aesthetic, rain-slicked industrial backdrop, neon glow reflection, sleek corporate design, detailed product photography, dark moody lighting, gritty cyberpunk cityscape below, minimalist interior, biometric scanner detail, wet pavement reflections, high contrast shadows
